title: work-conserving-linger-and-kv-prefetch-hints-for-continuous-batcher
author: Marina Cortez
description:
Motivation: tail latency for small interactive requests is driven by two opposing pressures: (1) batching/linger for throughput amortization and (2) strict fairness to avoid KV-heavy request starvation. This PR introduces a work-conserving linger window and lightweight KV-prefetch admission hints to reduce p99 for mixed workloads while preserving fairness guarantees.

High-level changes: add a configurable linger window at the continuous-batcher admission stage that is 'work-conserving' (i.e., dispatcher will not idle if there is inflight work on the device), implement an elastic lease recycler that returns unused slot reservations back to the admission pool earlier, instrument per-shard backlog watermarks used by admission smoothing (EWMA-backed), and introduce admission-level KV-prefetch hints that trigger async warming of shard-local KV caches for requests likely to need KV lookups. Also add kernel-hint tags that bias the runtime's kernel selector for short-sequence fast-paths when the admission signals low head-room.

Design details and safety knobs: linger window defaults to 2ms for high QPS routes and scales down under low backlog. Work-conserving mode ensures dispatch will immediately fill any free device cycles, avoiding dead time when linger expires and there are resource-compatible requests. Elastic lease recycler has a conservative timeout (linger * 3) to avoid chop. Admission smoothing uses a per-shard EWMA with a 200ms half-life to prevent rapid oscillation. KV-prefetch is opt-in per route via a new config flag (enable_kv_prefetch) and emits a prefetch telemetry event per request when triggered to avoid hidden cost. Kernel-hint tags are advisory only and cannot force a kernel; they tie into existing kernel-selection heuristics.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks run on a 4xA100 canary cluster with mixed workload (70% short-chat, 30% KV-lookup rerank). Compared to main on the same commit baseline: p50 unchanged, p95 improved 6%, p99 improved 14% for short-chat; end-to-end mixed-workload throughput improved 8% under 95th-percentile CPU pressure; KV-heavy request tail (p99) regressed by 2% when kv-prefetch is disabled, but with kv-prefetch enabled we saw a 9% improvement on kv-tail. See CI artifacts for full result matrices.

Migration and rollout: default is off for KV-prefetch; linger/work-conserving enabled behind route-level feature gates for canary. Rollout plan: internal canary -> 10% production (automated canary policy) -> 50% -> 100%. Monitoring: new metrics: continuous_batcher.linger_expired, continuous_batcher.reclaimed_leases, kv_prefetch.hits, kv_prefetch.bytes_warmed, kernel_hint.applied_rate, shard_backlog. Alerts added for unexpected lease churn and abnormal kv_prefetch cost.

Checklist: - [x] Unit + integration tests for linger/window edge cases - [x] End-to-end canary harness and benchmark scripts - [x] Runtime telemetry and dashboards - [x] Feature gate + operator docs - [x] Safety rollback (disable flags)

Why this is different from previous batching work: prior PRs focused on pure fairness or admission timeouts. This change aims to balance both by making short waits yield higher batching efficiency without ever leaving the device idle, and by warming KV caches opportunistically to reduce re-dispatch stalls.

Related: ENG-1259 (scheduler fairness followups), ENG-1304 (kv cache warmup design).

release_notes:
Introduce work-conserving linger window and opt-in KV-prefetch admission hints for continuous batcher. Improves p99 latency for mixed short-chat/KV workloads and adds operator knobs for EWMA backlog and lease recycling. KV-prefetch is off by default.

Operator action: review new metrics and enable feature gates gradually for canary routes.
notes_for_backport: No user-facing API changes. If backporting to 1.x release branch, backport dispatcher loop only with the lifecycle guard; kv-prefetch can remain a follow-on opt-in backport.
canary_plan: Deploy to canary cluster (gpu-a100-x4) with 5 routes enabled: 2 short-chat, 2 kv-rerank, 1 mixed. Run mixed_workload.yml bench for 30m, verify p95/p99 thresholds and monitor lease churn < 0.5% of requests.
docs_impact: docs/operators/continuous-batcher.md updated with new flags and metrics
